_comment: MCP config for pi-mcp-adapter, passed to pi as --mcp-config by
scripts/pi-local.sh. Absolute path, like every other resource this stack
hands pi, so it applies whatever directory pi was started in.
This is the pi side of the browser. The SERVER is not started from here:
scripts/browser.sh owns that process, so it outlives any one pi session and
can be shared. This file only says how to reach it and which of its 98 tools
are worth carrying as native pi tools.
${BROWSER_MCP_HOST} and ${BROWSER_MCP_PORT} are interpolated by the adapter
from the environment, which pi-local.sh exports out of .env — so the port
cannot drift from the one browser.sh binds. A missing variable fails before
any request is sent, rather than quietly resolving to a wrong URL.

_lifecycle: lazy: do not connect until a browser tool is actually called. The
server may legitimately be down for a whole session, and connecting at
startup would spend a failed request and a warning on every launch.
_requestTimeoutMs: Unset, this falls back to the MCP SDK default of 60 s. Measured
2026-08-16 on a session that hit a wedged Chrome: two navigate calls
each burned the full 60 s before the model gave up and fell back to
curl — two minutes of wall clock and ~500 tokens for a page it never
30 s is far above warm operation (25-417 ms per call through this
adapter; 3-32 s through the CLI, which pays process startup) and far
below the point where waiting is still useful. The cold case that used
to need the long timeout - a 74 s first Chrome launch - is gone:
browser.sh warms Chrome during `up` (BROWSER_MCP_WARM), so no client
_directTools: The browse loop, registered as ordinary pi tools so the model calls
them by name with a real schema instead of through the proxy. Measured
on the wire: 4,621 bytes, ~1,155 tokens for these five. The other 93
stay behind mcp({ search }) at no standing cost.
start_browser is deliberately NOT here: its schema alone is 2.3 KB
(~570 tokens, the largest on the server) and the server opens the
browser by itself on the first tool that needs one
(ZENDRIVER_MCP_AUTOSTART_BROWSER, set by browser.sh). Add it back only
if you need headless, a proxy, or a persistent profile chosen per call.
stop_browser is not here either — stopping is the process owner's job:

_outputGuard: The adapter's default cap is 50 KiB / 2,000 lines, which matches pi's
bash guard and is sized for a 200K window. Here it would be ~12.5k
tokens — 40% of a 32K window in one tool result. 8 KiB is ~2k tokens,
and the full text still lands in a temp file the model can read or grep
when it really needs the rest.
_freezeDirectTools: The registered tool surface is part of the prompt prefix, and this stack
reuses KV cache across turns and restarts (CACHE_PROMPT, CACHE_REUSE,
--slot-save-path). A reconnect that re-registers direct tools would
invalidate that prefix mid-session. The initial sync still runs.
_hostConfigDiscovery: Never adopt Cursor/Claude/Codex/Windsurf MCP configs found on the
machine. This box has several, and inheriting them would put servers in
the window that nobody chose for a 32K session.
